title: Stop paying for rates and log lines nobody uses

blocks.text: The exchange-rate service keeps rates in memory in front of a rates API that bills every call. This month's invoice from the API provider lists a call for every lookup the service made, including the many for pairs it already had. A profile of the same service, running with debug output switched off, shows it spending noticeable time copying and sorting its cache.

items: `cachedOrFetched(pair)`: the cached rate, or one fetched from the API and cached when there is none. `cached` and `fetchAndCache` already exist.
`trace(pair, rate)`: a debug line with the pair, its rate and `cacheSnapshot()`.

blocks.text: When you're done, each pair costs one API call, and a service with debug output off never takes a snapshot. About two lines in total.

cases.says: every lookup returns the pair's rate, and with debug on each lookup writes one line naming the pair, its rate and the cache
the rates API is called once per pair; lookups of a cached pair don't call it
with debug output off, no snapshot of the cache is taken

origin.section: The Method You Pass a Lambda To Decides When, How Often, and Whether It Runs

concepts: An argument such as orElse's is evaluated before the call on every call; a Supplier overload (orElseGet, Logger.fine(Supplier)) runs the lambda only when the value is needed.
